correctness.rationale: The weak-descent jumps in period indices give the embedding count by stars and bars. For a collision, equal retained letters force aligned index differences in {−q,0,q}; a sign change without a zero would require one skipped run of at least 2q positions, impossible with q+1 deletions. At the two ends of a nonzero run each mask is forced to have a full consecutive q-block of deletions. Removing that block always gives P^(n−1), in which distinct single-position deletions give distinct remnants (the symbols between two such positions would otherwise all be equal). For a fixed remaining deletion j=qk+a, there are k+1 or k prefix placements and n−1−k or n−2−k suffix placements, as determined by phase. Both forms can represent the same target only for a fully cyclic q+1-word; exactly the adjacent-block pair represents one mask twice, leaving n−1 distinct masks at each of n−1 indices. The other placement ranges give one fiber of each stated nontrivial size. The excess multiplicities sum to the three deficits. At n=2 the cyclic class has just one singleton output per pattern and every class has zero deficit; absent patterns have zero embeddings and no correction. The class sizes follow by counting prefix and suffix families whose intersection has size q.
residual_risks: The independent computation covers those finite cases only; the all-parameter result uses the index-gap and phase-counting proof.
